dedupe_keys.name: internet wide measurement of tls use in ten industrial protocols rwth aachen missed opportunities dataset

description: This dataset holds the measurement results and analysis scripts of an Internet-wide security assessment of ten industrial communication protocols over the whole IPv4 address space. The DataCite record says the study checked whether traditional industrial protocols retrofitted with TLS, such as Modbus, and modern protocols designed for TLS, such as MQTT, are actually deployed with TLS and configured to best practice, and the RWTH Publications page lists gzipped CSV files of certificates, host identifiers, current results, MQTT broker information and PeeringDB data, plus scan configuration, anonymisation, database schema and plotting archives. It was published in 2021 by six RWTH Aachen authors (Markus Dahlmanns, Johannes Lohmöller, Jan Pennekamp, Jörn Bodenhausen, Klaus Wehrle and Martin Henze) with the paper "Missed Opportunities: Measuring the Untapped TLS Support in the Industrial Internet of Things"; the files are downloadable from the record. Coverage is worldwide Internet-facing industrial devices. Caveats: the licence and file sizes are not stated on the page read, the page sits behind a browser check, and host data are anonymised. For simulation it gives the share of exposed industrial devices without secure communication, a prior for how many plants a remote attack could reach. Related catalogue records include ICSLibrary and the ICS advisories architectural weaknesses dataset.
